title: The GUM says the traditional ideas of error and of a true value focus on quantities that are unknowable
summary: The GUM says the traditional ideas of error and of a true value focus on quantities that are unknowable.
body: The Guide says the traditional concepts of error and of a true value of a measurand remain valid as ideals, but focus on unknowable quantities: the error of a result, and the true value as distinct from its estimate. The source says: "Although these two traditional concepts are valid as ideals, they focus on unknowable quantities: the “error” of the result of a measurement and the “true value” of the measurand (in contrast to its estimated value), respectively." The Guide's operational move is to evaluate uncertainty from the data and other information, not to claim that a measurement has revealed an unknowable true value. This is a statement about measurement language, not a denial that physical quantities exist.
said_by: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
